question: Who among the following proposed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​In order to** restrict the freedom of the Indian press**, British India passed the **Vernacular Press Act in 1878.**
 
• Its aim was to **suppress criticism of British policy**, especially the opposition that had grown since the **Second Anglo-Afghan War began (1878–80).**
 
• The Act was submitted by** Lytton, **the Viceroy of India at the time.
 
• On **March 14, 1878**, the** Viceroy's Council** unanimously approved it.
 
• It was decided to** "better govern"** the vernacular press by passing the** Vernacular Press Act (VPA).**
 
• With **"publications in eastern languages,**" the intention was to effectively **penalize and prohibit "seditious writing."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Lord Lytton was an experienced diplomat and a man of striking ability and brilliance.
 
• The British Prime Minister, Disraeli appointed him as the Viceroy of India.
 
• He acted as viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880.
 
• Events under Lord Robert Lytton's rule:
 
 
• The prevailing famine and the political disturbances in the northwest Frontier caused great worry to the British at that time. The first Famine Commission (1878-80) under Sir Richard Strachey was appointed and it made many commendable recommendations.
 
• In 1878, the Vernacular Press Act was passed.
 
• Lord Lytton introduced a uniform salt tax throughout British India. He also abolished many import duties and supported the Free Trade Policy
 
• Second Afghan War (1878-80): Soon after the outbreak of the war in 1878, the British troops captured the territory between Kabul and Kandahar. The ruler of Afghanistan, Sher Ali fled from his country and died in 1879. His son Yakub Khan became the ruler and the British concluded the Treaty of Gandamak with him.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon (11 January 1859 – 20 March 1925):**

 
 
• Lord Curzon was a prominent **British Conservative politician.**
 
• He presided over **India as Viceroy from 1899 until 1905.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Dufferin (21 June 1826 – 12 February 1902):**
 
 
• In 1884, Lord Dufferin was** India's Viceroy.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Lansdowne (14 January 1845 – 3 June 1927):**
 
 
• He was a **British statesman **who held the position of** Viceroy of India.**
